newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Settlers wound Arab woman in West Bank attack.
newsitem.headline: Settlers wound Arab woman in West Bank attack.

text.p: A Palestinian woman was shot and lightly wounded on Tuesday in a drive-by attack by Jewish settlers near the West Bank town of Hebron, Palestinian witnesses said.
Officials at Hebron's Alia hospital said Naziha Abu-Hmeid, 50, was in stable condition after being shot in the leg near Yatta village.
"While we were waiting on our land near the settlements, two settlers in a blue Subaru came and shot about 10 bullets towards us from their pistols," Ibrahim Abu Shakir, 55, told Reuters.
"I saw my wife fall down shouting. My son, who was about 50 metres (yards) from us, came immediately. The two settlers escaped in their car," Abu Shakir said.
Abu Shakir said he identified the gunmen as settlers by their long beards and skullcaps.
Israeli police were not immediately available for comment.

Hebron, holy to Jews and Moslems as the traditional burial place of the biblical patriarch Abraham, is a flashpoint of violence. In February 1994 Baruch Goldstein, a Jew from Kiryat Arba settlement adjacent to Hebron, shot dead 29 Arabs at prayer in the tomb, also known as al-Ibrahimi mosque. Survivors beat him to death.
Israeli and PLO negotiators are locked in talks on a long-delayed Israeli troop redeployment in Hebron.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu seeks to modify a Hebron deal signed by Israel's previous government to safeguard 400 Jewish settlers who live in the heart of Hebron among 100,000 Arabs.
Palestinians reject any changes to the deal.
Israeli security officials have said Israel would detain Jewish militants who might try to disrupt the handover of parts of Hebron to Palestinian self-rule.
